title: Rabbi Chiyya the Tall
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: [Ketubot 104b](https://www.sefaria.org/Ketubot.104b.8-13) relates that his mother-in-law was his brother’s wife; his brother died childless, and she summoned him to judgment before Rabbah bar Shila … he wrote her an authorization over his property. He came before Rava; Rabbi Chiyya the Tall said to him, “Let the Master see how they have judged me.” He said to him, “They judged you well.” The reading of the Rif and the Rosh is Rabbi Chiyya the Tall of Difti. In [Nedarim 8b](https://www.sefaria.org/Nedarim.8b.5): “Rabbi Shimon bar Zevid said that Rabbi Yitzchak bar Tavla said that Rabbi Chiyya the Tall said.” Hyman endorses [Heilprin’s question](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=1254&lang=en), since Rabbi Yitzchak bar Tavla was much earlier; he supports this by noting that Rabbi Shimon bar Zevid too lived in the days of Rabbi Zeira. Hyman considers the names there undoubtedly corrupted and suggests that the reference is to the Rabbi Chiyya who was tall in his generation.[^1]

notes.text: Ketubot gives twenty-five years of support. Rava upholds the ruling but finds the written authorization defective. Nedarim describes Chiyya the Tall as of the school of Rabbi Acha and continues the chain beyond him. Hyman reports the Difti reading of the Rif and Rosh and endorses Heilprin’s chronological difficulty.
